features.label: Human present-participle substantives
features.description: The two complete48-cell -ende systems use ordinary strong/weak adjective agreement. In40.5 hine ondrǣdendum, the participle is dative plural beneficiaries of mercy and hine its accusative object; om.on those rules out adding a demonstrative. In40.7 ðā hyngrendan, weak accusative plural identifies hungry people as the direct object of fill. A dative noun phrase is not an independent dative subject of fear, and hungry participles do not authorize personal finite hyngran.

features.label: Praise a person or entity
features.description: Hęrian takes the accusative praised person/entity. Imperative plural addresses the named beings; present third-plural subjunctive hęrien with hīe expresses let them praise. Indicative/imperative plural hęriað are syncretic, but syntactic roles are distinct.

features.label: Genitive request and wooing
features.description: Giernan governs the desired/requested thing or marriage partner in the genitive. Æt+dative identifies the person asked in39.3. The invariant relative ðe avoids demanding productive relative case attraction; the main-clause eall ðæt retains its own accusative object role.43.14’s genitive maiden is a marriage request, not a direct-object accusative.

features.label: Filling and material complements
features.description: Āfyllan takes an accusative entity and mid+dative contents. Its passive has the filled entity as nominative subject. Oferwyrcean38.1 independently takes the covered throne accusative and mid+dative gold. The shared case expression does not collapse the two lexical meanings.

features.label: Accept a person into care
features.description: Dative his cnihte Israel in40.8 extends the receiving frame to a person accepted/protected.39.6 edlēane uses the already taught dative thing received. BT attests accusative receiving elsewhere; an accusative is therefore not globally invalid, but does not instantiate the selected Cook164j dative frame.
